newsitem.title: TURKEY: Rival Iraqi Kurd groups resume talks in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Rival Iraqi Kurd groups resume talks in Turkey.

text.p: Rival Iraqi Kurdish groups began a further round of talks on Tuesday in a bid to forge a permanent peace in northern Iraq following a U.S.-brokered ceasefire last October.

The two days of talks between the delegations of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) were being overseen by U.S. mediator Robert Pelletreau and Turkish and British diplomats.
Participants say the two sides will try to agree on a ceasefire line in northern Iraq and a possible exchange of prisoners from several months of fighting last year.
The rival factions held talks in Washington last week.
There was no sign on Tuesday of PUK leader Jalal Talabani, who Turkish officials had said was expected to meet Pelletreau, an assistant secretary of state.
"The prospect emerged late (Monday) evening that he would not come," a Turkish foreign ministry official told Reuters. It was not immediately clear why Talabani did not attend the talks.
The KDP joined with Iraqi troops to take the key Kurdish city of Arbil from Talabani's fighters late last summer, prompting retaliatory U.S. missile strikes on Iraqi targets.
The clashes gave Baghdad a foothold in the Western-protected north of Iraq for the first time since the end of the 1991 Gulf War.
